examples.en: A famous guest appears on today's show.
The guests invited to the event went up on stage.

examples.ko: 이번 주 게스트는 제가 좋아하는 가수예요.
examples.en: This week's guest is a singer I like.
I was very nervous appearing on the radio as a guest.

examples.ko: 이 숙소는 게스트가 직접 요리할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Guests can cook for themselves at this lodging.

explain: '손님'은 집이나 가게에 온 모든 사람에게 쓰지만, 게스트는 방송 출연자, 행사에 초대받은 사람, 숙소 투숙객에게 더 많이 써요. 상대를 직접 높여 부를 때는 '손님'이 자연스러워요. 초대한 쪽은 '호스트'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 콘서트에 특별 게스트로 유명한 가수가 나왔어요.
phrases.en: A famous singer appeared as a special guest at the concert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 방송에 따로 초대해서 나온 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Someone specially invited to appear at an event or show.

phrases.en: I stayed at a guesthouse on my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행객이 싸게 머무는 작은 숙소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small, cheap lodging for travelers.

phrases.en: A guest came to our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 직접 부르거나 집·가게에 온 사람에게는 '손님'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Sonnim' is used to address someone or for people visiting a home or shop.

explain_en: '손님' covers anyone who comes to a home or shop, while 'guest' is used more for show guests, invitees at events and lodgers. When addressing someone directly, '손님' is more natural. The host side is '호스트'.

t90.ax: This week's guest is a singer I like.

examples.en: Our boss always comes to work early.
The boss suddenly called a meeting.
I beat the final boss in the game.
I told my boss about my vacation.
That person is the boss of this team.

explain: 회사에서 사장님이나 상사를 장난스럽게, 영어식으로 부르는 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '부장님', '팀장님'처럼 직함을 써요. 게임에서는 마지막에 싸우는 큰 적을 '보스'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I beat the final boss in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임 이야기에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in talk about games.

phrases.en: That person really seems like a boss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신감 있고 힘 있는 사람을 장난스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful way to describe a confident, commanding person.

phrases.en: The boss came early today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보스'보다 회사에서 더 정중하고 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More polite and standard at work than 보스.

explain_en: In a company it is a playful, English-style way to refer to the CEO or a superior. When addressing someone directly, use a title like 부장님 or 팀장님. In games, 보스 is the big enemy you fight at the end.

examples.en: My mother remarried, so I got a stepfather.
My stepfather treats me like his own son.
I go fishing with my stepfather.
Today is the day I greet my stepfather for the first time.
I decided to call my stepfather 'Dad'.

explain: '새아빠'보다 조금 정중하게 말할 때 써요. 법이나 서류에서는 '계부'라고 해요. 짝이 되는 말은 '새어머니'예요.

phrases.en: My stepdad plays with me every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새아버지'보다 편하고 가까운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual and familiar word than 새아버지.

phrases.en: I live with my stepfather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-와 함께'로 같이 지내는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -와 함께 tells who you live with.

phrases.en: It's the day I greet my stepfather for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높임말 '-께'를 붙여 존댓말로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the honorific -께 makes it respectful.

explain_en: It sounds a little more polite than '새아빠'. In legal or official documents the term is '계부'. Its counterpart is '새어머니'.

t90.ax: My stepfather's job is a chef.

examples.en: My uncle works at the same company as my aunt.
I went fishing with my uncle.

examples.ko: 설날에 이모부께 세배를 하고 용돈을 받았어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day I bowed to my uncle and got pocket money.

examples.ko: 이모부 집에 가면 항상 맛있는 음식이 많아요.
examples.en: When I go to my uncle's house, there's always lots of tasty food.

examples.ko: 이모부를 처음 만났을 때 많이 긴장했어요.
examples.en: I was very nervous when I first met my uncle.

explain: 이모의 남편은 '이모부', 아버지 여자 형제의 남편은 '고모부'라서 헷갈리지 않게 구분해요. 직접 부를 때는 '이모부님'처럼 높이기도 해요.

phrases.en: Uncle, have you eaten?
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부를 때는 '님'을 붙여 높여요.
phrases.nuance_en: When addressing him directly, add 'nim' to show respect.

phrases.en: My aunt and her husband sent me a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부부를 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the couple together.

phrases.en: My father's sister's husband runs a store with her.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아버지 여자 형제의 남편이라서 이모부와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: The husband of your father's sister, different from 'imobu'.

explain_en: Your maternal aunt's husband is 이모부, and your father's sister's husband is 고모부, so keep them apart. When addressing him directly, people sometimes raise it to '이모부님'.

t90.ax: I went fishing with my uncle.

examples.en: My friend's grandmother came up from the countryside yesterday.

examples.ko: 병원에서 할머님께 약 먹는 방법을 설명해 드렸어요.
examples.en: At the hospital I explained to the elderly lady how to take her medicine.
The elderly lady takes a walk every morning.
My friend's grandmother gave me a tasty snack.

explain: '할머니'에 높임말 '-님'을 붙인 말이에요. 자기 할머니는 보통 '할머니'라고 하고, 다른 사람의 할머니나 모르는 어르신께는 '할머님'이라고 높여요. 가게나 병원에서 나이 드신 여자 손님을 이렇게 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: My friend's grandmother came up from the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '께서'를 붙여 할머님이 주어일 때 높여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 께서 shows respect when the grandmother is the subject.

phrases.en: I greeted the elderly lady respectfully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '께'를 붙여 할머님에게 하는 행동을 높여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 께 respectfully marks the grandmother as the receiver of an action.

phrases.en: My grandmother lives in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 할머니를 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic word, used for your own grandmother.

explain_en: It is 할머니 plus the honorific -님. People call their own grandmother 할머니, and use 할머님 for someone else's grandmother or an elderly woman they don't know. Shops and hospitals also use it for older women customers.

t90.ax: Ma'am, if your legs hurt, please sit here.

examples.en: My shoelace came undone, so I tied it again.

examples.ko: 구두끈을 너무 꽉 묶으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: If you tie your shoelaces too tight, your feet hurt.
I almost tripped on my shoelace while running.
You have to make a strong knot in your shoelaces.
The length of the laces differs by shoe too.

explain: 구두에 달린 끈이에요. 운동화까지 포함해서 말할 때는 '신발끈'이 더 넓게 쓰여요. '끈을 묶다, 끈이 풀리다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: My shoelace came undone and I almost fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구두뿐 아니라 운동화 끈까지 넓게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers sneaker laces as well as dress shoe laces.

phrases.en: I tied my shoelaces before going to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈을 매듭지을 때 '묶다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 묶다 is the verb for tying laces.

phrases.en: My shoelace came undone while I was walking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묶은 끈이 저절로 풀릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tied lace comes loose by itself.

explain_en: This is the lace on dress shoes. When you mean laces on any shoes including sneakers, '신발끈' has a wider range. You say things like '끈을 묶다' (tie the lace) and '끈이 풀리다' (the lace comes undone).

en: to perform surgery; to operate on (a patient)

examples.en: I'm having surgery on my knee at the hospital next week.
The doctor operated for three hours.
My grandmother had eye surgery last month.
I rested for a week after the surgery.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 이 병은 수술해야 한다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said this condition needs surgery.

examples.ko: 무서워서 수술하기 전날 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I was scared and couldn't sleep the night before the surgery.

explain: 의사가 주어일 때도, 환자가 '다음 주에 수술해요'라고 말할 때도 다 써요. 환자 쪽을 분명히 하려면 '수술을 받다'를 써요. '무릎을 수술하다'처럼 몸 부위를 목적어로 쓰고, '수술이 잘됐어요'처럼 명사로도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My grandfather had knee surgery yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자 쪽에서 수술을 당했다는 점을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear that the speaker is the patient receiving surgery.

phrases.en: Fortunately, the surgery went well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '수술'을 써서 결과를 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '수술' to talk about how the surgery turned out.

phrases.en: The doctor said I need to have surgery on my leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수술이 꼭 필요하다는 말을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that surgery is necessary.

explain_en: It works when the doctor is the subject, and also when a patient says '다음 주에 수술해요' (I'm having surgery next week). To make the patient's side clear, use '수술을 받다' (undergo surgery). The body part can be the object, as in '무릎을 수술하다', and the noun is common too, as in '수술이 잘됐어요' (the surgery went well).

examples.ko: 윗집에 아이들이 이사 와서 집이 시끄러워졌어요.
examples.en: Children moved into the apartment above, so my home got noisy.

examples.ko: 윗집 소음 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep because of the noise from upstairs.
The person from upstairs came by and apologized in person.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫집'이고 아파트에서는 '위층', '아래층'이라고도 많이 말해요. 층간 소음 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. 어떤 집의 위에 있는 집을 가리키니까 '우리 윗집'처럼 기준이 되는 집이 있어야 해요.

phrases.en: A sound from upstairs woke me up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파트에서 윗집 대신 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in apartments instead of 'witjip'.

phrases.en: The person from the apartment above came to say hello.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 집에 사는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to the people living there.

phrases.en: I'm having a hard time because of the noise from the apartment above.
phrases.nuance_ko: 층간 소음 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about noise between floors.

explain_en: The opposite is '아랫집', and in apartments people also say '위층' and '아래층'. It comes up a lot when talking about noise between floors. It points to the home above a certain home, so it needs a reference, like '우리 윗집' (the home above ours).

t90.ax: I can't sleep because of the noise from upstairs.
